title: Effective-Geometry Rescaling and Universal Critical Behavior in the Anisotropic Three-State Potts Model on the Square Lattice
authors: Fan Yang, Jian Gao, Lu Liu, Yuhai Liu
abstract: We study the two-dimensional anisotropic three-state Potts ferromagnet on the square lattice using Wolff single-cluster Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling. For coupling ratios $λ=J_y/J_x=0.5$, $0.75$, and $1$, finite-size scaling of the correlation ratio yields critical behavior consistent with the two-dimensional three-state Potts universality class. The scaling of the leading Fisher zeros gives a correlation-length exponent consistent with $ν=5/6$, while their cumulative density is consistent with the expected specific-heat exponent $α=1/3$. We further characterize the anisotropy at criticality using directional correlation ratios $R_x$ and $R_y$ together with directional FK wrapping probabilities. For $λ=0.5$ on a physically square lattice, $R_x$ and $R_y$ approach distinct critical values while yielding a common correlation-length exponent. From the wrapping probabilities, we independently determine an effective aspect ratio $ρ_e^\square=0.6413(5)$, in close agreement with the theoretical value $ρ_e^{\square,\mathrm{th}}\simeq0.64150030$ obtained from the isoradial representation. Using the theoretical value to set the physical aspect ratio restores directional equivalence, $R_x\simeq R_y$, and brings the overall correlation ratio toward the isotropic-square reference. The results show that spatial anisotropy changes the effective critical geometry without altering the bulk three-state Potts universality class.
summary: This paper studies the anisotropic three-state Potts model on a square lattice to determine how spatial anisotropy affects its critical behavior. Using Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling, the authors show that while anisotropy alters the system's effective geometry, the underlying bulk critical universality class remains robustly that of the isotropic three-state Potts model.
main_problem: To investigate whether spatial anisotropy in the two-dimensional three-state Potts ferromagnet modifies the bulk critical universality class or primarily affects the finite-size critical geometry.
main_result: The study concludes that spatial anisotropy changes the effective critical geometry (e.g., directional correlation ratios) but does not alter the bulk critical universality class, which remains consistent with the 2D three-state Potts model.
method: The research employs Wolff single-cluster Monte Carlo simulations and finite-size scaling analysis, supplemented by the analysis of Fisher zeros and directional correlation ratios.
model_or_system: The system is an anisotropic three-state Potts ferromagnet defined on a square lattice with Hamiltonian $H = -\sum_{\langle ij angle_x} J_x \delta_{\sigma_i, \sigma_j} - \sum_{\langle ij angle_y} J_y \delta_{\sigma_i, \sigma_j}$. The anisotropy is controlled by the ratio $\lambda = J_y/J_x$.

paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the critical behavior using multiple diagnostic tools (FSS, Fisher zeros, directional ratios) to distinguish between universal bulk properties and non-universal geometric effects induced by anisotropy.
why_interesting: The work provides a detailed theoretical understanding of how lattice geometry and anisotropy manifest at criticality, offering a quantitative framework (effective-geometry rescaling) to separate universal physics from non-universal boundary effects.
